bull_case: AI/HPC demand lets TSMC deploy record capex at high utilization and strong margins, compounding FCF/share.
bear_case: If overseas fabs structurally dilute margins or AI capacity is overbuilt, high capex can depress FCF/share for years.
thesis: TSMC can absorb enormous internally generated capital at attractive returns. FY2025 OCF-capex was about US$32B and H1 2026 owner-style FCF before dividends was about US$20B. The main risk is that global-fab duplication raises capital intensity faster than incremental cash returns.

evidence.claim: FY2025 OCF was US$72.52B, capex about US$40.56B and R&D US$7.86B.
1H26 OCF was NT$1.482T and capex NT$846.76B.

counterevidence: Overseas fabs carry structurally higher costs; customer concentration and Taiwan/export-control tail risks remain material.
unknowns: AI/HPC demand duration beyond the current capacity-constrained cycle
falsifiers: A sustained loss of leading-edge share, repeated yield delays, or owner FCF/share stagnation despite rising capex would weaken the thesis.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current revenue, margin and cash-flow acceleration do not establish structural incremental-ROIC collapse.
TSMC has no evidence of long-running excessive equity dilution; share count is broadly stable and SBC is immaterial relative to cash generation.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth through the capex cycle

next_checks: 3Q26 results, N2 ramp, CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity, overseas-fab margin, top-customer concentration

subscores.rationale: Revenue, margin and cash generation have risen sharply alongside large leading-edge and packaging investments.
Capex+R&D absorbs well over 60% of OCF and AI/HPC/N2/packaging/global capacity provide a long runway.
FCF/share is growing but remains capex-cycle sensitive; H1 2026 FCF per ADR annualizes above 2025.

uncertainties.rationale: AI-cycle duration, overseas economics and geopolitical/customer concentration remain material uncertainties.
